## What it finds

A setting that lets an agent run any command, or skip its approval prompts, without asking you.
Each agent module knows its own syntax. The table below shows what counts for each agent.

| Agent | Over-broad permission |
|---|---|
| Claude Code | `Bash(*)` and other blanket shell rules, `bypassPermissions` |
| Codex | approval `never` together with `danger-full-access` |
| Cursor | `Shell(*)`, `approvalMode: unrestricted` |
| Gemini CLI | bare `run_shell_command`, a trusted MCP server |
| Windsurf | a command allow-list entry that approves any command (`bash`, an empty prefix) |
| OpenCode | `permission` set to `"allow"` for everything or for every shell command |
| GitHub Copilot | `allow-all`, VS Code `chat.tools.global.autoApprove` |
| Hermes Agent | `approvals.mode: off`, `hooks_auto_accept` |
| Antigravity | `always-proceed`, `command(*)` |

## Why it matters

With a blanket grant, one bad prompt or one poisoned file can make the agent run a command you
never saw. That command runs with your full permissions.

## How to fix

Remove the blanket grant. Allow only the specific commands or tools you need. Keep
approve-everything modes for throwaway containers or virtual machines.

## Limits

- Only the settings in the table are checked. Other agents' permission modes are not covered yet.
- Cursor's IDE auto-run mode lives inside its `state.vscdb` database and is not read yet.
- This is a medium print: a grant is a risk, not a leak.
